topic: Linea terminalis (arcuate line + ala margin) and pelvic inlet - author drawing
citation: Am J Biol Anthropol. 2021 Dec 29;177(4):690–707. doi: 10.1002/ajpa.24466
title: The morphological consequences of segmentation anomalies in the human sacrum
authors: Krenn V. A., Fornai C., Webb N. M. et al.

figures.label: FIGURE 1
figures.caption: (a) Drawing of the lower spine and the pelvis in anterior view illustrating the spatial relationships between the iliac crest and the fourth and fifth lumbar vertebrae, the linea terminalis, which is composed of the arcuate line and the margin of the pelvic brim on the ala of the first sacral vertebra (marked as “ala margin”). (b) Visualization of the categorial relationship between the iliac crest and the fourth (L4) and fifth (L5) lumbar vertebrae, namely (1) center of L4, (2) inferior surface of L4, (3) superior surface of L5, and (4) center of L5. (c) The trajectories from the arcuate line on the hipbones to the margin of the pelvic brim of the sacral alae. The pelvic inlet thereby forms a flat circular plane (2) but can also be elongated, bent upwards (1), or curtailed and bent downwards (3)
figures.what_it_shows: Panel (a): anterior-view line drawing of lower spine and pelvis; blue dashed line traces the linea terminalis on each side (iliac 'arcuate line' continuing onto the sacral 'ala margin' of S1), and a horizontal dashed line marks the iliac-crest level (L4/L5). Panels (b, c) are schematics of segmentation-anomaly levels (not needed for the lecture - crop to panel a).
figures.labels_visible_in_image: (a) T12, L4, L5, S1, 'Iliac crest', 'ala margin', 'arcuate line'; (b) 1, 2, 3, 4; (c) 1, 2, 3

label_points.latin: Linea terminalis, pars sacralis (margo alae sacri)

key_findings: 145 clinical CT scans. 'the trajectory of the margin of the pelvic brim onto the sacral alae (the iliac portion of linea terminalis) could either be (1) upwards, (2) straight, or (3) downwards with respect to the arcuate line'. 'Such a second promontory was found in 13 specimens with lumbosacral transitional vertebra (60%).'
clinical_relevance: Lumbosacral transitional vertebrae (sacralisation/lumbarisation) change the shape of the pelvic inlet and the position of the promontory - relevant to obstetric pelvimetry and spinal level counting.
notes: CC BY-NC (non-commercial) - flag. Drawing, not a photograph; promontorium, pecten ossis pubis and crista pubica are not labelled in the image - add Turkish labels manually only if an anatomist confirms. Crop to panel (a).

figures.what_it_shows: Two 3D-CT volume renderings of the pelvis (anterior view left, posterior-inferior view right) with numbered white lines: 1 transverse diameter of inlet, 2 biacetabular, 3 bispinous (between ischial spines), 4 bituberous (outlet), 5 subpubic angle.
figures.labels_visible_in_image: numbers 1, 2, 3, 4, 5; white measurement lines; dotted black lines

label_points.latin: Linea terminalis (end-point of transverse inlet diameter)

key_findings: 211 females, 181 males (CT). Table 1 (female vs male, mm): transverse inlet 135.0±8.5 vs 126.8±7.0; bispinous 112.2±9.2 vs 93.6±8.4; outlet (bituberous) 123.9±10.4 vs 103.5±9.3; sagittal inlet 124.6±10.3 vs 119.2±10.2; sagittal outlet 99.9±9.8 vs 96.0±7.4; 'Subpubic angle' 132±12 vs 94±12 degrees. 'The results demonstrated that more pronounced age-related changes occurred in the inlet and the outlet of the lesser pelvis. The mid-cavity was less changing.'
clinical_relevance: 'The pelvic floor dysfunction and the pelvic organ prolapse are observed more often in females with a wider ... and more horizontally oriented pelvic inlet ..., a wider distance between ischial spines ..., and a longer sagittal diameter of the outlet'.
notes: CC BY-NC - flag. Gives real male/female numbers for the 'pelvis feminina vs masculina' slide. Subpubic angle here measured on CT differently from PMC7118257 (values not interchangeable).

topic: Male vs female pelvis: subpubic angle on 3D-CT

authors: Mohd Ali S. H., Omar N., Shafie M. S. et al.

figures.label: Fig. 2
figures.caption: Three-dimensional computed tomography models of the pelvis showing landmarks in the study. (A) Male pelvis. (B) Female pelvis. L1 and L4, most inferior points on ischiopubic ramus; L2 and L3, most anteroinferior points on symphysis pubis.
figures.what_it_shows: Anterior-inferior 3D-CT views of a male (A) and female (B) pelvis with landmarks L1-L4 (inferior ischiopubic ramus points and anteroinferior symphysis points) and the subpubic angle arc - narrow male vs wide female pubic arch.
figures.labels_visible_in_image: A, B, L1, L2, L3, L4 (orange dots), white arc

key_findings: 50 male + 50 female MDCT. 'Results showed that the subpubic angle in males was 68.6°±7.6° and in females 87.4°±6.5°.' 'The overall accuracy of sex estimation using the subpubic angle was 94% (P<0.001). The subpubic angle, with a demarcating point of 78.6°, showed a sensitivity and specificity of 94% in the classification of female individuals.'
clinical_relevance: Subpubic angle is the classic male/female discriminator (angulus subpubicus vs arcus pubicus); population-specific cut-offs.
notes: CC BY-NC - flag. Best whole-pelvis male/female comparison found.

title: Importance of Sacrotuberous Ligament in Transgluteal Approach for Sciatic Nerve Entrapment in the Greater Sciatic Notch (Piriformis Syndrome)

figures.label: Fig. 1.
figures.caption: Changes in the extent of decompression of the sciatic nerve pathway during transgluteal sciatic nerve decompression. A : Extent of decompression of the sciatic nerve pathway via conventional method (black-dotted line circle). B : Circumferential dissection of the sciatic nerve performed more proximally than in the conventional method to decompress the compartment (red-dotted circle) composed of the sacrotuberous ligament, piriformis muscle, and sciatic nerve. STL : sacrotuberous ligament, Pfm : piriformis muscle, SN : sciatic nerve, PN : pudendal nerve.

figures.labels_visible_in_image: A, B, STL, Pfm, SN, PN; grey and red dotted circles

key_findings: 81 patients analysed (transgluteal sciatic decompression). 'sciatic nerve decompression was successful in 50 of 81 patients (61.7%)'. topic: Fascia obturatoria, arcus tendineus m. levatoris ani (ATLA) and arcus tendineus fasciae pelvis (ATFP) - cadaver hemipelvis

authors: Chin H. Y., Peng C. W., Wu M. P. et al.

figures.label: Figure 2
figures.caption: Photographs of the inner side of a hemipelvis with the intact obturator fascia. (A) The arcus tendinous levator ani (ATLA) is located within the obturator fascia and attached from the ischial spine to the inferior border of the superior ramus of the pubic bone. The arcus tendineus fasciae pelvis (ATFP) is located between the urinary bladder and obturator fascia and is attached from the ischial spine to the inferior border of the pubic symphysis (PS) in the right pelvis. (B) The obturator fascia can be separated from the obturator internus muscle through the obturator canal in the right pelvis. (C) The margins of the obturator fascia can also be identified through finger insertion into the space between the obturator fascia and obturator internus muscle in the left pelvis. (D) The obturator fascia in the left pelvis of male. (E) The thickness of obturator fascia of male is significantly thinner than that of female. The obturator canal is labeled by a circle. *p < 0.01.

Panel E = bar chart of obturator fascia thickness (male vs female).
figures.labels_visible_in_image: A-E, PS, ATLA, ATFP, black circles; bar chart axis 'Thickness of obturator fascia (mm)', male, female, *

Fascia obturatoria / fascia m. levatoris ani fusion
Fascia obturatoria / fascia m. levatoris ani fusion

key_findings: 10 embalmed cadavers (4 F, 6 M). 'the average thickness of obturator fascia in male (0.167 ± 0.031 mm) was thinner than in female (0.228 ± 0.036 mm) (Fig. 2E, p < 0.01, t-test).' 'Some skeletal muscle fibers were found above the ATLA within the obturator fascia ... the attachment of LAM aponeurosis extended beyond ATLA to the inferior border of the superior ramus of the pubic bone.'

topic: Levator ani architecture from serial sections: puborectal vs 'pubovisceral' parts, coccygeus (3D reconstruction)
title: 3D Topography of the Young Adult Anal Sphincter Complex Reconstructed from Undeformed Serial Anatomical Sections
authors: Wu Y., Dabhoiwala N. F., Hagoort J. et al.

figures.label: Fig 1
figures.caption: The architecture of the levator ani muscle.Panel G shows the positions of the transverse sections in panels A-D and that of obliquely sectioned panel E (calculated from reconstruction). The sections show the bilayered make-up of the pubovisceral muscle (A-C) and its attachment to the rectococcygeal muscle (A,B), the extension of the pubovisceral and deep layer of the puborectal muscles to the pubic bone (B,C), the external anal sphincter, the superficial layer of the puborectal muscle, and the conjoint longitudinal muscle of the rectum (C-E), and the rectoperineal muscle (D). Panel E visualizes the successive layers of the anal-sphincter complex, while panel F, a calculated midsagittal section of this specimen, shows the muscles surrounding the anal canal. Panels G and H show reconstructions of the levator and sphincter ani muscles as seen from the left (G) and anterosuperior (H). The color code of the (outlined) structures is shown in S2 Fig and sections without outlines S5 Fig. Abbreviations: AL, anococcygeal ligament; Ant, anterior; B, bladder; Co, coccygeal muscle; EAS, external anal sphincter; GM, gluteus maximus muscle; Post, posterior; PR-D, puborectal muscle, deep portion; PR-S, puborectal muscle, superficial portion; PV, pubovisceral muscle with deep (purple) and superficial (orange) layers; RC, rectococcygeal muscle; U, urethra; R, rectum; V, vagina.
figures.specimen: 3D reconstruction from undeformed serial anatomical sections (Chinese Visible Human, real cadaver sections)
figures.what_it_shows: A-E transverse/oblique and F midsagittal cryosection images with outlined muscles; G left-lateral and H anterosuperior 3D reconstructions of levator ani subdivisions: coccygeus (Co), pubovisceral (PV, bilayered), puborectal (PR), rectococcygeal (RC), obturator internus (OI), external anal sphincter (EAS). Use panel H (and G) only for the topographic lecture.
figures.labels_visible_in_image: A-H; Ant, Post, B, U, V, R, OI, GM, P, EAS, Fat; G: Co, RC, PV, AL, PR-D, PR-S, EAS, Ant, red lines A-E; H: Co, RC, PV, OI, E-A-S, PR

key_findings: 6 young adults (4 F, 2 M). 'we observed no perimysial septa between puborectal and pubococcygeal portions that would allow a separation as shown in virtually all textbooks.' 'The LAM had a common anterior attachment to the pubic bone, but separated posteriorly into puborectal and "pubovisceral" muscles.' 'The pubovisceral muscle comprised the pubo- and iliococcygeal muscles that are shown in most atlases'. 'the post-mortem levator hiatus was ~61 mm longer and ~23 mm narrower, and had descended 3–5 mm more ... than measured in life'. Attachment to the obturator internus ('tendinous' arch) 'was remarkably inconspicuous'.
clinical_relevance: Challenges the textbook three-part levator ani; puborectal loops define the levator (urogenital) hiatus - relevant to obstetric levator avulsion and continence.
notes: CC BY. Panels A-F are cross-sections (deck is topographic) - crop to G/H. Shared folder: the anal-triangle agent may reference the same figure.

figures.caption: Visualizations: pubovisceral muscle origin in bright red, pubovaginal muscle insertion in dark red, puboperineal muscle insertion in orange, puboanal muscle insertion in yellow, puborectal muscle origin and insertion in green, iliococcygeus muscle origin and insertion in blue, coccygeus muscle insertion in gray
